findings.description: The instance user_data script exports a plaintext AWS access key ID and secret access key (`AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID=AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMAAA`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=...`). These credentials are stored in source control, in Terraform state, and are readable by anyone with describe-instance-attributes or access to instance metadata, so they must be treated as compromised.
The security group opens SSH (port 22) to 0.0.0.0/0, exposing remote shell access to the entire internet and enabling brute-force or credential-stuffing attacks against the instance.
The egress rule allows all protocols to 0.0.0.0/0, giving the instance an unrestricted outbound channel for data exfiltration and command-and-control communication.
map_public_ip_on_launch is true, so every instance launched in this subnet (including the portal server) receives a publicly routable IP address by default, exposing it directly to the internet.
map_public_ip_on_launch is true, so instances launched into this subnet automatically receive public addresses and are reachable from the internet regardless of intent.
The EBS volume has no `encrypted = true` (nor a KMS key), so the attached disk and its snapshots are stored unencrypted and readable by any principal with access to the underlying storage.
The snapshot is created from an unencrypted volume and does not set `encrypted = true`, so the backup leaves a plaintext copy of the disk data that persists independently of the source volume.
The S3 bucket storing VPC flow logs has no server-side encryption configuration, so the archived network traffic metadata is stored unencrypted at rest.
force_destroy = true permits the bucket and all retained flow-log history to be deleted without a safeguard, undermining the audit trail and enabling an attacker to destroy evidence of activity.

A default route to the internet gateway in `portal_routes` makes any subnet associated with that route table (both portal subnets) internet-routable, so the workload's resources are directly reachable from and able to reach the public internet.
